## Document structure

This document contains the tests for the Matter application clusters, complementing the tests for the Matter core features documented in Matter Core Test Plan. Please refer to Matter Core Test Plan for sections Introduction, Definitions, Test Setup and Platform Certification.

## Chapter 1. On/Off Cluster Test Plan

## 1.1. PICS Definition

This section covers the On/Off Cluster Test Plan related PICS items that are referenced in the following test cases. Support for an item is considered as "true" for conditional statements within the test case steps.

## 1.1.1. Role

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| OO.S | Does the device implement the On/Off Cluster as a server? | O | |
| OO.C | Does the device implement the On/Off Cluster as a client? | O | |

## 1.1.2. Server

## Features

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| OO.S.F00(LT) | Does the device implement "Lighting" feature? | [!OO.S.F02(OFFONLY)] | |
| OO.S.F01(DF) | Does the device implement "DeadFrontBehaviour" feature? | [!OO.S.F02(OFFONLY)] | |
| OO.S.F02(OFFONLY) | Does the device implement "OffOnly" feature? | [!(OO.S.F00(LT)&#124;OO.S.F 01(DF))] | |

## Attributes

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| OO.S.A0000(OnOff) | Does the device implement the OnOff attribute? | OO.S:M | |

| OO.S.A4000(GlobalScen eControl) | Does the device implement the OO.S.A4000(GlobalScen eControl) attribute? | OO.S.F00(LT) |
| OO.S.A4001(OnTime) | Does the device implement the OnTime attribute? | OO.S.F00(LT) |
| OO.S.A4002(OffWaitTi me) | Does the device implement the OffWaitTime attribute? | OO.S.F00(LT) |
| OO.S.A4003(StartUpOn Off) | Does the device implement the StartUpOnOff attribute? | OO.S.F00(LT) |

## Manual controllable

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| OO.M.ManuallyControll ed | Can the OnOff attribute changed by physical control at the device? | OO.S : O | |

## Commands received

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| OO.S.C00.Rsp(Off) | Does the device implement receiving the Off command? | OO.S:M | |
| OO.S.C01.Rsp(On) | Does the device implement receiving the On command? | !OO.S.F02(OFFONLY) | |
| OO.S.C02.Rsp(Toggle) | Does the device implement receiving the Toggle command? | !OO.S.F02(OFFONLY) | |
| OO.S.C40.Rsp(OffWithEf fect) | Does the device implement receiving the OffWithEffect command? | OO.S.F00(LT) | |

| OO.S.C41.Rsp(OnWithR ecallGlobalScene) | Does the device implement receiving the OnWithRecallGlobalSce ne command? | OO.S.F00(LT) |
| OO.S.C42.Rsp(OnWithTi medOff) | Does the device implement receiving the OnWithTimedOff command? | OO.S.F00(LT) |

## 1.1.3. Client

## Commands generated

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| OO.C.C00.Tx(Off) | Does the device implement sending the Off command? | OO.C:O | |
| OO.C.C01.Tx(On) | Does the device implement sending the On command? | OO.C:O | |
| OO.C.C02.Tx(Toggle) | Does the device implement sending the Toggle command? | OO.C:O | |
| OO.C.C40.Tx(OffWithEff ect) | Does the device implement sending the OffWithEffect command? | OO.C:O | |
| OO.C.C41.Tx(OnWithRe callGlobalScene) | Does the device implement sending the OnWithRecallGlobalSce ne command? | OO.C:O | |
| OO.C.C42.Tx(OnWithTi medOff) | Does the device implement sending the OnWithTimedOff command? | OO.C:O | |

## 1.2. PIXIT Definition

This section covers the On/Off Cluster's Test Plan related PIXIT items that might be required in the following test cases.

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| PIXIT.OO.ENDPOINT | Endpoint supported for On/Off Cluster and Level Control is given by the DUT Manufacturer | [!OO.S.F02(OFFONLY)] | For TC-2.5 execution Level Control and On/OffControl cluster must exist on the same endpoint |

## 1.3. Test Case List

| TC UUID | Test Case Name |
| TC-OO-2.1 | Attributes with server as DUT |
| TC-OO-2.2 | Primary functionality with server as DUT |
| TC-OO-2.3 | Secondary functionality with server as DUT |
| TC-OO-2.4 | Startup functionality with server as DUT |
| TC-OO-2.5 | DeadFrontBehaviour Feature with DUT as Server - PROVISIONAL |
| TC-OO-2.6 | OffOnly Feature with DUT as Server |
| TC-OO-2.7 | Scenes Management Cluster Interaction (DUT as Server) |
| TC-OO-3.2 | Functionality with client as DUT |

## 1.3.1. Notes/Testing Considerations

- In test cases where a change in an attribute value is tested over time, it is permitted for the devices involved in the test to be within a tolerance of ±15% of the expected time or value, on top of PIXIT.OO.MaxCommunicationTurnaround.

## 1.4. Test Cases

## 1.4.1. Server as DUT

## TC-OO-2.1 Attributes with server as DUT

## Purpose

This test case verifies that the DUT can respond to on/off cluster attribute read commands.

## · OO.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | | | Commission DUT to TH | |
| 4 | | OO.S.A4 001(On Time) | TH reads the OnTime attribute from the DUT | • Verify that the DUT responds with a uint16 value. • Save the value as 'initial-On- time' |
| 5 | | OO.S.A4 001(On Time) | TH writes the OnTime attribute as 30 | Verify that the DUT sends success response |
| 6 | | OO.S.A4 001(On Time) | TH reads the OnTime attribute from the DUT | Verify that the DUT responds with value 30 |
| 7 | | OO.S.A4 001(On Time) | TH writes the OnTime attribute as 'initial-On-time' to restore the original value | Verify that the DUT sends success response |

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 8 | | OO.S.A4 002(Off WaitTi me) | TH reads the OffWaitTime attribute from the DUT | • Verify that the DUT responds with a uint16 value. • Save the value as 'initial-Off- waittime' |
| 9 | | OO.S.A4 002(Off WaitTi me) | TH writes the OffWaitTime attribute as 30 | Verify that the DUT sends success response |
| 10 | | OO.S.A4 002(Off WaitTi me) | TH reads the OffWaitTime attribute from the DUT | Verify that the DUT responds with value 30 |
| 11 | | OO.S.A4 002(Off WaitTi me) | TH writes the OffWaitTime attribute as 'initial-Off-waittime' to restore the original value | Verify that the DUT sends success response |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

## TC-OO-2.3 Secondary functionality with server as DUT

## Purpose

This test case verifies the secondary functionality of the on/off cluster server. This test case is only required if the Level Control for Lighting feature is supported (OO.S.F00(LT)).

## PICS

- OO.S
- OO.S.F00(LT)

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

Commission DUT to TH

## TC-PCC-2.5 Reporting requirements with DUT as Server - PROVISIONAL

## Purpose

This test case verifies the reporting requirements for Capacity , Speed and Power attributes of the Pump Configuration and Control Cluster server.

## · PCC.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | TH as Client. |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server. |

## Spec References

AC.4.2.7

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH (can be skipped if done in a preceding test).

## Test Procedure

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 2 | TH reads from the DUT the ServerList attribute on Descriptor cluster | Verify that the DUT response contains the ServerList attribute. |
| 3 | If DUT is supporting the Level Control cluster, TH reads from the DUT the MaxLevel attribute on Level Control cluster and store the value as maxLevel | Verify that the DUT response contains the MaxLevel attribute. |
| 4 | If DUT is supporting the Level Control cluster, TH sends command MoveToLevelWithOnOff with Level field set to maxLevel and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 5 | If DUT is not supporting LevelControl, TH sends command On command on OnOff cluster | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 7 | Set up a subscription wildcard subscription for the Pump Configuration and Control Cluster, with MinIntervalFloor set to 0, MaxIntervalCeiling set to 30 and KeepSubscriptions set to false | Subscription successfully established |

| 8 | TH counts all incoming reports for the Capacity attribute, that contains data, over a period of 30 seconds and store the count in numberOfCapacityReportsReceived | |
| 9 | TH verifies that numberOfCapacityReportsReceived is not higher than 30 | numberOfCapacityReportsReceived is less then or equal to 30 |
| 11 | TH counts all incoming reports for the Speed attribute, that contains data, over a period of 30 seconds and store the count in numberOfSpeedReportsReceived | |
| 12 | TH verifies that numberOfSpeedReportsReceived is not higher than 30 | numberOfSpeedReportsReceived is less then or equal to 30 |
| 14 | TH counts all incoming reports for the Power attribute, that contains data, over a period of 30 seconds and store the count in numberOfPowerReportsReceived | |
| 15 | TH verifies that numberOfPowerReportsReceived is not higher than 30 | numberOfPowerReportsReceived is less then or equal to 30 |
| 16 | TH sends command Off command on OnOff cluster | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

Given it is not possible to force a device into setting the attributes to null, the requirement of:

- Changes from null to any other value and vice versa

is currently not validated in this test case.

## 9.3. Test Cases

## 9.3.1. Low Power Cluster Test Cases

## TC-LOWPOWER-2.1 Low Power Mode Verification (DUT as Server)

## Purpose

This test case verifies the low power cluster server functionality

## PICS

- LOWPOWER.S

## Spec References

{REF\_LOWPOWER}.4 - Refer to the *Low Power Cluster Commands* section.

## Preconditions

| # | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | DUT is powered on and not in a low power state | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH, if not done so already. In some cases, such as with a Casting Video Player, the DUT commissions the TH.

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | TH sends Sleep command to DUT | Verify response is a successful (value 0x00) status response and that the device enters its low power state. |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

1. Refer to manufacturer provided instructions for special argument values to each command, and/or additional steps required to put DUT into correct state to exhibit test behavior.

## TC-LOWPOWER-2.2 Low Power Mode Verification (DUT as Client)

## Purpose

This test case verifies that the DUT can send a low power command

## PICS

- LOWPOWER.C

## Spec References

{REF\_LOWPOWER}.4 - Refer to the *Low Power Cluster Commands* section.

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as server |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as client |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission TH to DUT, if not done so already. In some cases, such as with a Casting Video Client, the TH commissions the DUT.

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | | LOWPO WER.C. C00.Tx( Sleep) | DUT sends Sleep command to TH | Verify command is successfully received by TH |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

1. Refer to manufacturer provided instructions for special argument values to each command, and/or additional steps required to put DUT into correct state to exhibit test behavior.

## 9.3.2. KeyPad Input Cluster Test Cases

## TC-KEYPADINPUT-3.1 Send Key Command Verification (DUT as Client)

Purpose

This test case verifies that the DUT can send a SendKey command

PICS

## TC-APPLAUNCHER-3.8 Stop Application Verification

## Purpose

This test case verifies stopping of a specified application

## PICS

- APPLAUNCHER.S

({REF\_APPLAUNCHER}.6 &amp; {REF\_APPLAUNCHER}.7) - Refer to the *Application Launcher Cluster Commands* section.

## Preconditions

| # | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | DUT is powered on and not in a low power state | |
| 2 | DUT supports one or more apps | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH, if not done so already. In some cases, such as with a Casting Video Player, the DUT commissions the TH.

## Test Procedure

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | TH sends a LaunchApp command to DUT to launch and bring an application to the foreground | The DUT should respond with a LauncherResponse command with Status set to Success (0), confirming the application launched successfully. If data field present, include Optional app-specific data. The Status attribute of the launched application's endpoint in the Application Basic cluster should be updated to ACTIVE_VISIBLE_FOCUS. |

| 2 | TH sends a StopApp command to DUT to stop a running application | The DUT should respond with a LauncherResponse command with Status set to Success (0), indicating the application was successfully stopped. If present, the Data field may contain optional information relevant to the stop operation. The Status attribute of the corresponding endpoint in the Application Basic cluster should be updated to STOPPED, confirming the app is no longer running or visible. |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

1. Refer to manufacturer provided instructions for special argument values to each command, and/or additional steps required to put DUT into correct state to exhibit test behavior.

## 9.3.5. Wake-On LAN Test Cases

## TC-WAKEONLAN-4.1 Wake-On LAN Verification

## Purpose

This test case verifies that the device can wake up from a low-power state using the Wake-On LAN standard

## PICS

## · WAKEONLAN.S

## Spec References

AC.1.11.2 - Refer to the Wake On LAN Cluster Attributes section.

## Preconditions

| # | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | DUT is powered on and not in a low power state | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH, if not done so already. In some cases, such as with a Casting Video Player, the DUT commissions the TH.

## Test Procedure

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | WAKEO NLAN.S. A0000(M ACAddre ss) | TH reads the MACAddress attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response contains a 48- bit MAC Address. Record the MAC address. |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 3 | | TH sends a Wake-On LAN magic packet containing the MAC address from step 1 | Verify that the DUT is no longer in a low-power state. |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

1. If the device does not support the MAC Address attribute, then the MAC address can be acquired by other means (network scans, device documentation, etc) for step 3.
2. If the device does not support the Low Power cluster (LOWPOWER.S), then the DUT can be put to sleep using other means for step 2. Latest commit d4a89ef on Dec 10, 2021
3. To verify a device has woken up, any Matter cluster command can be send to the device (for example, read descriptor cluster at endpoint 1).
4. Refer to manufacturer provided instructions for special argument values to each command, and/or additional steps required to put DUT into correct state to exhibit test behavior.

## 9.3.7. Media Playback Test Cases

## TC-MEDIAPLAYBACK-6.1 Mandatory Media Playback Verification

## Purpose

This test case verifies the mandatory commands for the Media Playback cluster (Play, Pause, Stop)

## PICS

- MEDIAPLAYBACK.S

## Spec References

## (AC.6.10.6 &amp; AC.6.10.7) - Refer to the Media Playback Cluster Attributes and Commands section.

## Preconditions

| # | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | DUT is powered on and not in a low power state | |
| 2 | DUT has media content available for playback | |
| 3 | Media content is loaded/selected and in a paused state at the beginning of the content (PlayBackPosition 0) | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH, if not done so already. In some cases, such as with a Casting Video Player, the DUT commissions the TH.

## Test Procedure

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PAUSED" |
| 2 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C00. Rsp(Play ) | TH sends a Play command to the DUT | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media state is playing. |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 3 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PLAYING" |
| 5 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PAUSED" |
| 6 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C02. Rsp(Stop ) | TH sends a Stop command to the DUT | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media state is stopped. Refer to manufacturer provided instructions for the expected physical DUT behavior for the stop command. |
| 7 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "NOT_PLAYING" |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

1. Manufacturer should provide information on the desired behavior for the stop command in step 6 (ex: should the user be navigated back to a home screen).
2. Manufacturer may provide instructions for how to verify media playback state.
3. Manufacturer may provide instructions for how to put media state into precondition state. With the example tv-app, state can be set to paused using the pause command:

chip-tool mediaplayback pause 1234 3

## TC-MEDIAPLAYBACK-6.2 Optional Media Playback Verification

## Purpose

This test case verifies the optional commands for the Media Playback cluster (StartOver, Previous, Next, SkipForward, and SkipBackward)

## PICS

## · MEDIAPLAYBACK.S

## Spec References

(AC.6.10.6 &amp; AC.6.10.7) - Refer to the Media Playback Cluster Attributes and Commands section.

## Preconditions

| # | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | DUT is powered on and not in a low power state | |
| 2 | DUT has media content available for playback | |
| 3 | Media content is loaded/selected and in a paused state at the beginning of the content (PlayBackPosition 0) | |
| 4 | At least 2 media items are queued | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH, if not done so already. In some cases, such as with a Casting Video Player, the DUT commissions the TH.

## Test Procedure

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PAUSED" |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 3 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PLAYING" |
| 5 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C05. Rsp(Nex t) | TH sends a Next command to the DUT | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the next media item in the queue has been loaded (see manufacturer defined behavior) |
| 6 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C04. Rsp(Prev ious) | TH sends a Previous command to the DUT | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the previous media item in the queue has been loaded (see manufacturer defined behavior) |
| 7 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C08. Rsp(Skip Forward | TH sends a SkipForward command to the DUT with a DeltaPositionMilliseconds value of 10000 | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media has skipped forward 10 seconds |
| 8 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 3(Sampl edPositi on) | TH reads the SampledPosition attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a position of 10000 |
| 9 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C09. Rsp(Skip Backwar | TH sends a SkipBackward command to the DUT with a DeltaPositionMilliseconds value of 10000 | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media has skipped backward 10 seconds |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 10 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 3(Sampl edPositi on) | TH reads the SampledPosition attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a position of 0 |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

1. Manufacturer should provide information on the desired behavior for the next and previous commands in steps 5 and 6 respectively (ex: should the experience progress to the previous/next item in a media queue?)
2. If a skip (steps 7 and 9) falls in the middle of a frame, the device must set the position to the beginning of that frame. Physical measurements and SampledPosition reads may not exactly reflect the number of skipped milliseconds.
3. Manufacturer may provide instructions for how to verify media playback state.

## PICS

## · MEDIAPLAYBACK.S

(AC.6.10.6 &amp; AC.6.10.7) - Refer to the Media Playback Cluster Attributes and Commands section.

## Preconditions

| # | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | DUT is powered on and not in a low power state | |
| 2 | DUT has media content available for playback | |
| 3 | Media content is loaded/selected and in a paused state at the beginning of the content (PlayBackPosition 0) | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |

| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Test Procedure

| 1 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C0b. Rsp(Seek ) | TH sends a Seek command to the DUT with a Position value of 10000 | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media has moved to 10 seconds from the starting point. |
| 2 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 3(Sampl edPositi on) | TH reads the SampledPosition attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a position of 10000 |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PAUSED" |
| 2 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 4(Playba ckSpeed) | TH reads the PlaybackSpeed attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a PlaybackSpeed of 0 |
| 3 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C07. Rsp(Fast Forward ) | TH sends a FastForward command to the DUT | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media state is playing. |
| 4 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PLAYING" |
| 5 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 4(Playba | TH reads the PlaybackSpeed attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a PlaybackSpeed of 1 |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 7 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 4(Playba | TH reads the PlaybackSpeed attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a PlaybackSpeed of 2 |
| 9 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 0(Curren tState) | TH reads the CurrentState attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a playback status of "PLAYING" |
| 10 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 4(Playba ckSpeed) | TH reads the PlaybackSpeed attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a PlaybackSpeed of -1 |
| 11 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C06. Rsp(Rew ind) | TH sends a Rewind command to the DUT | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media play speed has increased in the reverse direction. |
| 12 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 4(Playba ckSpeed) | TH reads the PlaybackSpeed attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a PlaybackSpeed of -2 |
| 13 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C00. Rsp(Play ) | TH sends a Play command to the DUT | Verify that a successful (status 0) response is received and verify that the media is has resumed playing forward at the default speed. |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 14 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.A000 4(Playba ckSpeed) | TH reads the PlaybackSpeed attribute from the DUT | Verify that the response has a PlaybackSpeed of 1 |
| 15 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C07. Rsp(Fast Forward ) | TH sends consecutive FastForward commands up to the manufacturer defined max speed | Verify that a SPEED_OUT_OF_RANGE (status 4) response is received. |
| 16 | MEDIAP LAYBAC K.S.C06. Rsp(Rew ind) | TH sends consecutive Rewind commands up to the manufacturer defined max speed | Verify that a SPEED_OUT_OF_RANGE (status 4) response is received. |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

1. Manufacturer should provide values for the maximum fast-forward and rewind speeds for steps 15 and 16
2. Manufacturer may provide instructions for how to verify media playback state.

| 1 | APBSC.S. A0000(V endorNa me) | TH reads the VendorName attribute from the DUT | Verify the VendorName attribute value as follows: The value shall be a human-readable (displayable) string specifying the vendor's name. The length shall not exceed 32 UTF-8 characters. If not explicitly set, the attribute shall default to an empty string (""). |

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |

The CatalogVendorID should be an unsigned 16-bit integer of the vendor ID of the catalog, which should be either a CSA issued ID or 0x0000 if it is the DIAL catalog. ## TC-LVL-2.3 Reporting requirements with DUT as Server

## Purpose

This test case verifies the reporting requirements for CurrentLevel and RemainingTime attributes of the Level Control Cluster server.

## PICS

## · LVL.S

## Required Devices

| Device Name | Device Description |

| 1 | TH | TH as Client. |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server. |

## Spec References

## AC.1.6.6

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH (can be skipped if done in a preceding test).

## Test Procedure

| # | TestStep | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | Commission DUT if not already done | |
| 2 | TH reads FeatureMap attribute and the AttributeList value | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |
| 3a | If the MaxLevel attribute is in the AttributeList, TH reads MaxLevel attribute and store value as maxLevel, otherwise set maxLevel to 254 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |
| 3b | If the MinLevel attribute is in the AttributeList, TH reads MinLevel attribute and store value as minLevel, Otherwise, set minLevel to 0 if the LT (LVL.S.F01) feature is not supported, or to a value of 1 if LT is supported, as defined by the specification. | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |
| 4 | TH sends the command MoveWithOnOff with MoveMode field set to Down and rate set to 254 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |
| 5 | TH reads CurrentLevel attribute and store value as startCurrentLevel | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |
| 6 | Set up a subscription wildcard subscription for the Level Control Cluster, with MinIntervalFloor set to 0, MaxIntervalCeiling set to 30 and KeepSubscriptions set to false | Subscription successfully established |
| 7 | TH sends the command MoveToLevelWithOnOff with Level field set to maxLevel, TransitionTime field set to 100 (10s) and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |

| 8 | TH stores the reported values of CurrentLevel in all incoming reports for CurrentLevel attribute, that contains data in reportedCurrentLevelValuesList, over period of 30 seconds. | a |
| 9 | TH verifies that reportedCurrentLevelValuesList does not contain more than 12 entries for CurrentLevel | reportedCurrentLevelValuesList has 12 or fewer entries in the list |
| 10 | If reportedCurrentLevelValuesList only contain a single entry, TH verifies the value of the entry is equal to maxLevel | The entry in reportedCurrentLevelValuesList is equal to maxLevel |
| 11 | If reportedCurrentLevelValuesList contains two or more entries, TH verifies the value of the first entry is larger than startCurrentLevel | The first entry in reportedCurrentLevelValuesList is equal to or larger than to startCurrentLevel |
| 12 | If reportedCurrentLevelValuesList contains two or more entries, TH verifies the value of the last entry is equal to maxLevel | The last entry in reportedCurrentLevelValuesList is equal to maxLevel |
| 13 | If the LT feature is not supported, skip remaining steps and end test case | |
| 16 | TH sends the command MoveToLevel with Level field set to startCurrentLevel, TransitionTime field set to 100 (10s) and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |
| 17 | Wait for 5 seconds | |
| 18 | TH sends the command MoveToLevel with Level field set to startCurrentLevel, TransitionTime field set to 150 (15s) and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS |
| 19 | Wait for 20 seconds | |
| 20 | TH verifies reportedRemainingTimeValuesList contains three entries | reportedRemainingTimeValuesList has 3 entries in the list |
| 21 | TH verifies the first entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is approximately 100 (10s) | The first entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is in the range 95 - 100 |

| 22 | TH verifies the second entry reportedRemainingTimeValuesList approximately 150 | The second entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is in the range 145 - 150 |
| 23 | TH verifies the third entry reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is 0 | The third entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is equal to 0 |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

Given it is not possible to force a device into setting the attributes to null, the requirement of:

- Changes from null to any other value and vice versa

is currently not validated in this test case.

## NOTE

CurrentFrequency is not being validated, due to the Frequency feature being provisional.

## TC-LVL-3.1 MoveToLevel Verification (DUT as Server)

## Purpose

This test case verifies the MoveToLevel and MoveToLevelWithOnOff command functionality

## PICS

- LVL.S

## Preconditions

| # | Doc. Ref. | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | | DUT is powered on and not in a low power state | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

- Commission DUT to TH, if not done so already.

- For commands used in steps 1-4 of this test, use fields OptionsMask=0x00 and OptionsOverride=0x00.
- For the steps 5 and beyond, use fields OptionsMask and OptionsOverride as specified in the test steps.
- The levels used in this test assume that MinLevel=1 and MaxLevel=254. For DUTs that have different values, adapt the values used accordingly.

## Test Procedure

## Chapter 11. Color Control Cluster Test Plan

## Tolerance allowance

In test cases where a change in an attribute value is tested over time, it is permitted for the devices involved in the test to be within a tolerance of ±15% of the expected time.

Also, when reading attributes representing a color value, they may deviate from the value provided in a related command due to rounding effects in DUT, inaccuracies during a transition (±15% value tolerance allowed), or due to clipping if the value provided in the command is outside the support range of the DUT.

## 11.1. PICS Definition

This section covers the Color Control Cluster Test Plan related PICS items that are referenced in the following test cases. Support for an item is considered as "true" for conditional statements within the test case Steps.

## 11.1.1. Role

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| CC.S | Does the device implement the Color Control Cluster as a server? | O | |
| CC.C | Does the device implement the Color Control Cluster as a client? | O | |

## 11.1.2. Server

## Features

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| CC.S.F00(HS) | Does the DUT(server) support the "Hue/Saturation" feature? | CC.S: EHUE, O | |
| CC.S.F01(EHUE) | Does the DUT(server) support the "Enhanced Hue" feature? | CC.S: CL, O | |

| CC.S.F02(CL) | Does the DUT(server) support the "Color Loop" feature? | CC.S:O |
| CC.S.F03(XY) | Does the DUT(server) support the "Color XY" feature? | CC.S:O |
| CC.S.F04(CT) | Does the DUT(server) support the "Color Temperature" feature? | CC.S:O |

## Attributes

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| CC.S.A0000(CurrentHue ) | Does the device implement the CurrentHue attribute? | CC.S.F00(HS) | |
| CC.S.A0001(CurrentSatu ration) | Does the device implement the CurrentSaturation attribute? | CC.S.F00(HS) | |
| CC.S.A0002(RemainingT ime) | Does the device implement the REMAININGTime attribute? | CC.S:O | |
| CC.S.A0003(CurrentX) | Does the device implement the CurrentX attribute? | CC.S.F03(XY) | |
| CC.S.A0004(CurrentY) | Does the device implement the CurrentY attribute? | CC.S.F03(XY) | |
| CC.S.A0005(DriftCompe nsation) | Does the device implement the DriftCompensation attribute? | CC.S: O | |

This test case verifies the ColorControl Cluster attributes with server as DUT

PICS

· CC.S

| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Test Procedure

| Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |

| 1 | | Commission DUT to TH | |
| 2 | CC.S.A0 000(Cur rentHu e) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0000) CurrentHue attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint8 |
| 3 | CC.S.A0 001(Cur rentSat uration ) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0001) CurrentSaturation attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint8 |
| 4 | CC.S.A0 002(Re mainin gTime) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0002) RemainingTime attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint16 |
| 5 | CC.S.A0 003(Cur rentX) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0003) CurrentX attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint16 [Min:0 Max:0xfeff] |
| 6 | CC.S.A0 004(Cur rentY) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0004) CurrentY attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint16 [Min:0 Max:0xfeff] |
| 7 | CC.S.A0 005(Dri ftComp ensatio n) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0005) DriftCompensation attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains a enum8 [Min:0 Max:4] |
| 8 | CC.S.A0 006(Co mpensa tionTex t) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0006) CompensationText attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains a string [Max:254] |
| 9 | CC.S.A0 007(Col orTemp erature Mireds) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0007) ColorTemperatureMireds attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint16 [Min:1 Max:0xfeff] |
| 10 | CC.S.A0 008(Col orMode ) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x0008) ColorMode attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an enum8 [Min:0 Max:2] - 0 CurrentHue and CurrentSaturation - 1 CurrentX and CurrentY |

| 11 | CC.S.A0 00f(Opt ions) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x000f) Options attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains a bitmap8 - 0 None - 1 Other / Unknown - 2 Temperature monitoring - 3 Optical luminance monitoring and feedback - 4 Optical Color monitoring and feedback |
| 12 | CC.S.A4 000(En hanced Current Hue) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x4000) EnhancedCurrentHue attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint16 |
| 13 | CC.S.A4 001(En hanced ColorM ode) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x4001) EnhancedColorMode attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains a enum8 - 0 CurrentHue and CurrentSaturation - 1 CurrentX and CurrentY - 2 ColorTemperatureMireds - 3 EnhancedCurrentHue and CurrentSaturation |
| 14 | CC.S.A4 002(Col orLoop Active) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x4002) ColorLoopActive attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint8 |
| 15 | CC.S.A4 003(Col orLoop Directio n) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x4003) ColorLoopDirection attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint8 |
| 16 | CC.S.A4 004(Col orLoop Time) | TH reads from the DUT the (0x4004) ColorLoopTime attribute | Verify that the DUT response contains an uint16 |

## TC-CC-2.2 Reporting requirements with DUT as Server

## Purpose

This test case verifies the reporting requirements for ColorTemperatureMireds , CurrentHue , CurrentSaturation , CurrentX , CurrentY , EnhancedCurrentHue and RemainingTime attributes of the Color Control Cluster server.

## PICS

- CC.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | TH as Client. |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server. |

## Spec References

AC.3.2

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH (can be skipped if done in a preceding test).

## Test Procedure

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | Commission DUT to TH (can be skipped if done in a preceding test). | |
| 4 | TH reads from the DUT the ServerList attribute on Descriptor cluster | Verify that the DUT response contains the ServerList attribute. |

| 5 | If OnOff cluster is present in ServerList , TH sends command On command on OnOff cluster | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 6 | Set up a subscription wildcard subscription for the Color Control Cluster, with MinIntervalFloor set to 0, MaxIntervalCeiling set to 30 and KeepSubscriptions set to false | Subscription successfully established |
| 7 | If the CT feature is not supported on the cluster, skip step 8 to 12 | |
| 8 | TH sends command MoveColorTemperature with MoveMode field set to Down, Rate field set to 65535 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 9 | TH reads from the DUT the ColorTempPhysicalMaxMireds and stores the returned value as colorTempPhysicalMaxMireds | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 10 | TH sends command MoveToColorTemperature with ColorTemperatureMireds field set to the value of colorTempPhysicalMaxMireds , TransitionTime field set to 100, remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 11 | TH stores the reported values of ColorTemperatureMireds in all incoming reports for ColorTemperatureMireds attribute, since step 10, that contains data in reportedColorTemperatureMiredsValuesList , over a period of 20 seconds. | |
| 12 | TH verifies that reportedColorTemperatureMiredsValuesList does not contain more than 12 entries for ColorTemperatureMireds | reportedColorTemperatureMiredsValuesList has 12 or less entries in the list |
| 13 | If the HS feature is not supported on the cluster, skip step 14 to 21 | |
| 14 | TH sends command MoveHue with MoveMode field set to Down, Rate field set to 255 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 15 | TH sends command MoveSaturation with MoveMode field set to Down, Rate field set to 255 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |

| 16 | TH sends command MoveToHue with Hue field set to 254, TransitionTime field set to 100, Direction field set to Shortest and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 18 | TH verifies that reportedCurrentHueValuesList does not contain more than 12 entries for CurrentHue | reportedCurrentHueValuesList has 12 or less entries in the list |
| 19 | TH sends command MoveToSaturation with Saturation field set to 254, TransitionTime field set to 100 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 20 | TH stores the reported values of CurrentSaturation in all incoming reports for CurrentSaturation attribute, since step 19, that contains data in reportedCurrentSaturationValuesList , over a period of 20 seconds. | |
| 21 | TH verifies that reportedCurrentSaturationValuesList does not contain more than 12 entries for CurrentSaturation | reportedCurrentSaturationValuesList has 12 or less entries in the list |
| 22 | If the XY feature is not supported on the cluster, skip step 23 to 28 | |
| 23 | TH sends command MoveToColor with ColorX field set to 32768, ColorY set to 19660, TransitionTime field set to 0 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 24 | TH sends command MoveToColor with ColorX field set to 13107, ColorY set to 13107, TransitionTime field set to 100 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |

| 27 | TH verifies that reportedCurrentXValuesList does not contain more than 12 entries for CurrentX | reportedCurrentXValuesList has 12 or less entries in the list |
| 28 | TH verifies that reportedCurrentYValuesList does not contain more than 12 entries for CurrentY | reportedCurrentYValuesList has 12 or less entries in the list |
| 29 | If the EHUE feature is not supported on the cluster, skip step 30 to 32 | |
| 30 | TH sends command EnhancedMoveToHue with EnhancedHue field set to 0, TransitionTime field set to 100, Direction field set to Shortest and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 31 | TH stores the reported values of EnhancedCurrentHue in all incoming reports for EnhancedCurrentHue attribute, since step 30, that contains data in reportedEnhancedCurrentHueValuesList , over a period of 20 seconds. | |
| 32 | TH verifies that reportedEnhancedCurrentHueValuesList does not contain more than 12 entries for EnhancedCurrentHue | reportedEnhancedCurrentHueValuesList has 12 or less entries in the list |
| 34 | TH sends command MoveColorTemperature with MoveMode field set to Down, Rate field set to 65535 and remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |

| 36 | TH sends command MoveToColorTemperature with ColorTemperatureMireds field set to the value of colorTempPhysicalMaxMireds / 2, TransitionTime field set to 100, remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 37 | Wait for 5 seconds | |
| 38 | TH sends command MoveToColorTemperature with ColorTemperatureMireds field set to the value of colorTempPhysicalMaxMireds , TransitionTime field set to 150, remaining fields set to 0 | Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) |
| 39 | Wait for 20 seconds | |
| 40 | TH verifies reportedRemainingTimeValuesList contains three entries | reportedRemainingTimeValuesList has 3 entries in the list |
| 41 | TH verifies the first entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is approximately 100 | The first entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is in the range of 95 to 100 |
| 42 | TH verifies the second entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is approximately 150 | The second entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is in the range of 145 to 150 |
| 43 | TH verifies the third entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is 0 | The third entry in reportedRemainingTimeValuesList is equal to 0 |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

Given it is not possible to force a device into setting the attributes to null, the requirement of:

- Changes from null to any other value and vice versa

is currently not validated in this test case.

## Chapter 12. Occupancy Sensing Cluster Test Plan

## 12.1. PICS Definition

This section covers the Occupancy Sensing Cluster Test Plan related PICS items that are referenced in the following test cases. Support for an item is considered as "true" for conditional statements within the test case steps.

## 12.1.1. Role

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| OCC.S | Does the device implement the Occupancy Sensing Cluster as a server? | O | |
| OCC.C | Does the device implement the Occupancy Sensing Cluster as a client? | O | |

## 12.1.2. Server

## Features

## 12.3.2. Functional Tests

## TC-OCC-2.2 OccupancySensorTypeBitmap and OccupancySensorType interdependency with server as DUT

## Purpose

This test case verifies the OccupancySensorTypeBitmap and OccupancySensorType interdependency of the Occupancy Sensing Cluster server. For the compatibility of the server feature flag value, it can be found from the table from the spec section of "OccupancySensorType and OccupancySensorTypeBitmap Attributes". For example, if the server's feature flag value is PIR0 US-1 PHY-0, then value of OccupancySensor Type will be UltraSonic and its OCC.S.A0001(OccupancySensorType) attribute value will be 1 according to OccupancySensorTypeEnum Type.

## PICS

- OCC.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | | | Commission DUT to TH | |
| 2 | | OCC.S.A 0001(Oc cupanc ySensor Type) | TH reads OccupancySensorType attribute from DUT | Verify OccupancySensorType is set to one of the non-reserved values: 0-PIR, 1-Ultrasonic, 2-PIR and ultrasonic, and 3-Physical contact. |
| 3 | | OCC.S.A 0002(Oc cupanc ySensor TypeBit map) | TH reads OccupancySensorTypeBitmap attribute from DUT | Verify the value of OccupancySensorTypeBitmap and OccupancySensorType are aligned |

## TC-OCC-2.3 HoldTime Backward Compatibility Test with server as DUT

## Purpose

This test case verifies the Occupancy Sensing Cluster backward compatibility with 9 legacy timing attributes when a client supports a global cluster revision of less than 5, and the server supports OCC.S.A0003(HoldTime) attribute. If a server doesn't support OCC.S.A0003(HoldTime) attribute, then the server shall not support 9 legacy timing attributes.

## PICS

- OCC.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness as client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | | | Commission TH to DUT | |
| 6a | | | If DUT FeatureMap has PIR or (!PIR & !US & !PHY), and PIROccupiedToUnoccupiedDelay is supported, then TH writes HoldTimeMin to DUT's HoldTime attribute, otherwise skip 6a, 6b. | Verify that both PIROccupiedToUnoccupiedDelay attribute value and HoldTime attribute value are same as HoldTimeMin. |

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 8b | | | TH writes DUT PhysicalContactOccupiedToUnoccu piedDelay attribute with HoldTimeMax, then TH reads DUT PhysicalContactOccupiedToUnoccu piedDelay and HoldTime attributes. | Verify that both PhysicalContactOccupiedToUnoccu piedDelay attribute value and HoldTime attribute value are same as HoldTimeMax. |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

Sensor with single sensing modality is considered.

This section covers the Thermostat Cluster related PICS items that are referenced in the following test cases.

## 16.1.1. Role

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| TSTAT.S | Does the device implement the Thermostat Cluster as a server? | O | |
| TSTAT.C | Does the device implement the Thermostat Cluster as a client? | O | |

## Category

Functional conformance

## Purpose

This test case verifies the non-global attributes of the Thermostat Cluster cluster server.

## · TSTAT.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | TH as Client. |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server. |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH (can be skipped if done in a preceding test).

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | | | Commission DUT to TH (can be skipped if done in a preceding test). | |

| 9 | TSTAT. S.A0010 (LocalT empera tureCali bration ) | TH reads from the DUT the LocalTemperatureCalibration attribute. | Verify that the DUT response contains a SignedTemperature value. |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

Test Steps 3, 4, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 22, 26 and 30 to 62 cannot be executed with V1.0 SDK

The MaxThermostatSuggestions, ThermostatSuggestions, CurrentThermostatSuggestion, ThermostatSuggestionNotFollowingReason attributes are not tested here because TC-TSTAT-4.3 covers testing these attributes.

| 2 | If the ThreadMetrics attribute is supported, read the ThreadMetrics attribute | The data type in each field of the struct must match the value listed in the specification(s) Table in 11.12.6.1 ThreadMetrics Struct. The Id field of the list is mandatory and shall match with Node assigned ID unique-per-thread. Name field shall be set to vendor specific strings. Functional

## Chapter 28. Actions Cluster Test Plan

## 28.1. PICS Definition

This section covers the Actions Cluster related PICS items that are referenced in the following test cases.

## 28.1.1. Role

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| ACT.S | Does the device implement the Actions Cluster as a server? | O | |
| ACT.C | Does the device implement the Actions Cluster as a client? | O | |

## 28.1.2. Server

## Attributes

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| ACT.S.A0000(ActionList) | Does the device implement the ActionList attribute? | ACT.S:M | |
| ACT.S.A0001(EndpointL ists) | Does the device implement the EndpointLists attribute? | ACT.S:M | |
| ACT.S.A0002(SetupURL) | Does the device implement the SetupURL attribute? | ACT.S: O | |

## Manual controllable

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| ACT.S.M.FillActionList | Can the ActionList attribute be filled or changed by some means? (see Note) | ACT.S : O | Supporting the ActionList attribute is Mandatory. Providing a way to manually fill or update it is optional. |

| ACT.S.M.OverlappingEn dpointLists | Does the DUT support exposing an Endpoint in multiple EndpointListStructs | ACT.S : O | Supporting the EndpointLists attribute is Mandatory. Providing a mechanism to expose a particular Endpoint in multiple entries is optional. |
| ACT.S.M.SetupURLWith Suffix | Can a suffix be used on ACT.S.A0002(SetupURL) ? | ACT.S.A0002(SetupURL) : O | |

## NOTE

These 'manual' changes could be done be by manual control at the device or other manufacturer provided means, e.g. an app which has some proprietary interface into the server allowing to change the set of exposed groups and/or actions.

## TC-DESC-2.2 Descriptor Cluster Duplicate Condition with DUT as Server

## Purpose

This test case verifies the properties of Descriptor Cluster Attributes when the duplicate condition exists.

## PICS

- DESC.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | TH as Client. |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server. |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH.

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | 9.2, 9.5.4.1, 9.5.4.4, 9.5.4.5 | TH reads from the DUT the DeviceTypeList and PartsList attributes, and the TagList attribute if supported, for each endpoint supported by DUT | An endpoint that has a PartsList count greater than 0 is a parent endpoint. Identify all the tree-pattern style parent endpoints on the device. Omit any endpoint with the Content App device type. For each endpoint in this list, repeat steps 1-3 below: 1. For each child endpoint in the PartsList of the parent endpoint, for each device type in the DeviceTypeList of each child endpoint, add the child endpoint to a device type list containing endpoints of that device type. ◦ This yields an overview of which child endpoint(s) support which device type(s) for the parent endpoint. ◦ These device type lists are used in step 2. 2. For each device type list that contains more than one child endpoint, ◦ Verify that each child endpoint in the device type list supports the TagList feature in its descriptor cluster feature map. ◦ Verify that each child endpoint in the device type list has a TagList in its descriptor cluster. ◦ Verify that the set of tags in the TagList of each child endpoint in the device type list is not identical to the set of tags in the TagList of the other child endpoints in the device type list regardless of the ordering of the tags in each TagList . 3. Discard the device type list(s). |

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 2 | 9.2, 9.5.4.1, 9.5.4.4, 9.5.4.5 | | Identify all the children of the root node endpoint. | Repeat steps 1 to 3 of step 1 above for the direct children of the root node endpoint. |

## TC-DESC-2.3 Test for superset application device types DUT as Server

## Purpose

Test validates that application devices types are not listed on the root node endpoint and multiple non-superset application device types do not appear on a single endpoint.

## PICS

- DESC.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | TH as Client. |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server. |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Specification Reference

{REF\_ENDPOINT\_COMPOSITION} - Endpoint composition

## Test Procedure

| # | TestStep | Expected Outcome |
| 0 | TH performs a wildcard read of all attributes on all endpoints on the device | |
| 1 | TH checks the Root node endpoint and ensures no application device types are listed | No Application device types on EP0 |
| 2 | For each non-root endpoint on the device, TH checks the DeviceTypeList of the Descriptor cluster and verifies that all the listed application device types are part of the same superset, and that no two device types are unrelated supersets of any device type. | |

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1a | | | TH reads the ServerList attribute from the Descriptor cluster on EP0 | |
| 1b | | | If the ServerList contains the Time Synchronization Cluster ID, TH sends the SetUTCTime command with the UTCTime set to current epoch-us time and Granularity set to 3(MillisecondsGranularity). If the ServerList does not contain the Time Synchronization cluster ID, set TimeSyncSupported to False. | |
| 1c | | | If the ServerList contains the Time Synchronization cluster ID, TH reads the Time Synchronization cluster's UTCTime attribute on Endpoint 0. If UTCTime is present and non-null, then set TimeSyncSupported to True. Else set TimeSyncSupported to False | |
| 2 | | | TH reads the UpTime attribute from the DUT. Save the value in UpTime1 | Verify that UpTime1 is greater than 0. |
| 3 | | | If TimeSyncSupported is True, Run steps 3a - 3e | |
| 3a | | | TH reads the UTCTime attribute from the Time Synchronization cluster. Save it in UTCTime1 | Verify that the UTCTime value is not null. |

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 3c | | | TH sends a TimeSnapshot command to the DUT. | Verify that the DUT sends a TimeSnapshotResponse with the following conditions met: • Value of PosixTimeMs field is not null. • Value of (SystemTimeMs field / 1000) is greater than or equal to UpTime1. • PosixTimeMs field converted to a UTC timestamp is greater than or equal to UTCTime1 converted to a UTC timestamp. On success of prior verifications: • Save the value of the SystemTimeMs field as SystemTimeMs1. • Save the value of the PosixTimeMs |
| 4 | | | If TimeSyncSupported is False, Run steps 4a-4c. | |

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 4a | | | TH sends a TimeSnapshot command to the DUT. | Verify that the DUT sends a TimeSnapshotResponse with the following fields: • Value of PosixTimeMs field is null. • Value of (SystemTimeMs field / 1000) is greater than or equal to UpTime1. On success of prior verifications, save the value of SystemTimeMs field as SystemTimeMs1. |

## TC-DGGEN-3.1 Matter Specification 1.2 errata [DUT as Server]

## PICS

## · DGGEN.S

## Purpose

The AverageWearCount attribute of the General Diagnostics cluster was accidentally introduced in the 1.2 SDK, but was not added to the specification. This is therefore considered to be a nonstandard attribute in the standard range, but it will NOT be caught by the automated check process because it is present in the tools. This test verifies that this attribute is not present on the DUT.

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |

| 1 | TH | Test Harness as Client |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

Commission DUT to TH

## Test Procedure

| # | Ref | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | | | Commission DUT to TH | |
| 2 | | | TH reads the AttributeList global attribute from the DUT | Verify that the list does not include attribute ID 0x09 |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

In future iterations of the spec, this attribute ID will be marked as disallowed, which will flag this attribute automatically in the conformance tests. At that point, this test case can be removed.

## TC-CGEN-2.2 ArmFailSafe command verification [DUT as Server]

## Purpose

1. Verify that the failsafe expires without external intervention at PIXIT.CGEN.FailsafeExpiryLengthSeconds
2. Verify that sending an ArmFailSafe command with the ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to 0 causes an immediate expiry of the failsafe

3. Verify that disarming the failsafe resets the breadcrumb
4. Verify that the failsafe cannot be armed over a CASE session while the commissioning window is open
5. Verify that successfully establishing a PASE session causes the failsafe to arm
6. Verify that a successful CommissioningComplete command call persists the failsafe context
7. Verify that a successful CommissioningComplete command disarms the failsafe
8. Verify that a second admin cannot arm a failsafe while it is already held
9. Verify that sending a second ArmFailSafe command resets the timer

## PICS

## · CGEN.S

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | DUT | Server |
| 2 | TH1 | Client |
| 3 | TH2 | Client |

C.11.10.6.2 - ArmFailSafe

C.11.10.5.1 - Breadcrumb

C.11.18 - Operational credential

{REF\_CODE}.5.5 - Commissioning flow

TH1 and DUT are on the same fabric

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | TH1 reads the TrustedRootCertificates attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster and saves the number of list items as numTrustedRootsOriginal | |
| 2 | TH1 reads the BasicCommissioningInfo attribute and saves the MaxCumulativeFailsafeSeconds as maxFailsafe | |

| 3 | TH1 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to PIXIT.CGEN.FailsafeExpiryLengthSeconds and the Breadcrumb value as 1 | Verify that the DUT responds with ArmFailSafeResponse with ErrorCode as 'OK'(0) and DebugText argument is of type string with max length 512 or empty |
| 4 | TH1 reads the Breadcrumb attribute | Verify that the breadcrumb attribute is 1 |
| 5 | TH1 obtains or generates a new TrustedRootCertificate that is different from the previously commissioned TrustedRootCertificate for TH1. TH1 sends an AddTrustedRootCertificate command to the Node Operational Credentials cluster to install this new certificate | Verify that the DUT responds with SUCCESS |
| 6 | TH1 reads the TrustedRootCertificates attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster | Verify that the number of items in the returned list is numTrustedRootsOriginal + 1 |
| 7 | TH1 sends an ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to 1 and the Breadcrumb value as 2 | TH1 then waits 1 seconds to ensure the failsafe timer has expired |
| 8 | TH1 reads the TrustedRootCertificates attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster | Verify that the number of items in the returned list is numTrustedRootsOriginal |
| 9 | TH1 reads the Breadcrumb attribute | Verify that the breadcrumb attribute is 0 |
| 10 | TH1 repeats steps 3 through 5 | |
| 11 | TH1 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to 0 | Verify that the DUT responds with ArmFailSafeResponse with ErrorCode as 'OK'(0) and DebugText argument is of type string with max length 512 or empty |
| 12 | Repeat steps 8 through 9 | |
| 13 | TH1 sends the OpenCommissioningWindow command to the Administrator Commissioning cluster | Verify that the DUT returns a status code of SUCCESS |
| 14 | TH1 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to PIXIT.CGEN.FailsafeExpiryLengthSeconds | Verify that the DUT responds with ArmFailSafeResponse with ErrorCode as BusyWithOtherAdmin |
| 15 | TH2 opens a PASE session with the DUT | Verify that TH2 successfully opens a PASE session |

| 16 | TH2 obtains or generates a TrustedRootCertificate that is different from the previously commissioned TrustedRootCertificate for TH1. TH2 sends an AddTrustedRootCertificate command to the Node Operational Credentials cluster to install this new certificate | Verify that the DUT responds with SUCCESS |
| 17 | TH2 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to 0 | Verify that the DUT responds with ArmFailSafeResponse with ErrorCode as 'OK'(0) and DebugText argument is of type string with max length 512 or empty |
| 18 | TH1 reads the NOCs attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster using a non-fabric-filtered read and saves the returned list as nocs | |
| 19 | TH1 reads the Fabrics attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster using a non-fabric-filtered read and saves the returned list as fabrics | |
| 20 | TH1 reads the TrustedRootCertificates attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster and saves the returned list as trustedroots | |
| 21 | TH2 starts commissioning the DUT. It performs all steps up to establishing a CASE connection, but DOES NOT send the CommissioningComplete command | |
| 22 | TH2 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to 0 | Verify that the DUT processes the ArmFailSafe command and raises an exception due to incomplete commissioning |
| 23 | TH1 reads the NOCs attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster using a non-fabric-filtered read | Verify that the returned list matches nocs |
| 24 | TH1 reads the Fabrics attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster using a non-fabric-filtered read | Verify that the returned list matches fabrics |
| 25 | TH1 reads the TrustedRootCertificates attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster | Verify that the returned list matches trustedroots |
| 26 | TH2 fully commissions the DUT | Verify that the commissioning completes successfully |

| 27 | TH2 obtains or generates a new TrustedRootCertificate that is different from the previously commissioned TrustedRootCertificate for TH2. TH2 sends an AddTrustedRootCertificate command to the Node Operational Credentials cluster to install this new certificate | Verify that the DUT responds with FAILSAFE_REQUIRED |
| 28 | TH1 reads the Fabrics attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster using a non-fabric-filtered read | Verify that the returned list includes an additional entry for TH2 when compared to fabrics |
| 29 | TH1 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to PIXIT.CGEN.FailsafeExpiryLengthSeconds and the Breadcrumb value as 1 | Verify that the DUT responds with ArmFailSafeResponse with ErrorCode as 'OK'(0) and DebugText argument is of type string with max length 512 or empty |
| 30 | TH1 obtains or generates a new TrustedRootCertificate that is different from the previously commissioned TrustedRootCertificate for TH1. TH1 sends an AddTrustedRootCertificate command to the Node Operational Credentials cluster to install this new certificate | Verify that the DUT responds with SUCCESS |
| 31 | TH1 reads the TrustedRootCertificates attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster | Verify that the number of items in the returned list is numTrustedRootsOriginal + 2 |
| 32 | TH1 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to maxFailsafe | Verify that the DUT responds with ArmFailSafeResponse with ErrorCode as 'OK'(0) and DebugText argument is of type string with max length 512 or empty |
| 33 | TH1 waits for PIXIT.CGEN.FailsafeExpiryLengthSeconds | |
| 34 | TH1 reads the TrustedRootCertificates attribute from the Node Operational Credentials cluster | Verify that the number of items in the returned list is still numTrustedRootsOriginal + 2 |
| 35 | TH2 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to PIXIT.CGEN.FailsafeExpiryLengthSeconds and the Breadcrumb value as 1 | Verify that the DUT responds with ArmFailSafeResponse with ErrorCode as BusyWithOtherAdmin |
| 36 | TH1 sends ArmFailSafe command to the DUT with ExpiryLengthSeconds field set to 0 | |

If SupportedTemperatureUnits is not supported, TH creates a supported list with Celsius and Fahrenheit. ## TC-LTIME-3.1 Read and Write Time Format Localization Cluster Attributes [DUT as Server]

## Purpose

This test case verifies the read and write functionality of attributes provided by the Time Format

## PICS

## · LTIME.S

## Pre-Conditions

| # | Doc. Ref. | Condition |
| 1 | | TH is commissioned with DUT |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | DUT | DUT as Server |
| 2 | TH | Test Harness as Client |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission TH to DUT.

## Test Procedure

| # | TestStep | Expected Outcome |
| 0 | TH is commissioned with DUT | |
| 1 | TH reads HourFormat attribute from DUT | Verify that the HourFormat attribute is of Enum8 datatype and that the values are 0 (12hr), 1 (24hr), and 255 (UseActiveLocale) as per the HourFormatEnum in the specification. |
| 2 | TH writes 0(12hr) to HourFormat attribute | |
| 4 | TH writes 1(24hr) to HourFormat attribute | |
| 6 | TH writes 255 (UseActiveLocale) to HourFormat attribute | |

| 9 | TH reads the feature map attribute. If the CALFMT feature is not supported, skip all remaining steps | |
| 10 | TH reads SupportedCalendarTypes attribute from DUT and saves as cluster_supported_calendar_types | Verify that the SupportedCalendarTypes attribute is of Enum8 datatype and only contains values from 0-11 (specific calendar types) and 255 (UseActiveLocale), as defined in the CalendarTypeEnum in the specification. |
| 11 | TH reads ActiveCalendarType attribute from DUT | Verify that the ActiveCalendarType is in cluster_supported_calendar_types |
| 12 | For each entry in cluster_supported_calendar_types , TH writes that value to ActiveCalendarType, verifies that the write was successful and confirms the value via a read | Write is successful and read value matches for every entry |
| 13 | TH finds the set of CalendarTypesEnum value that do not appear in cluster_supported_calendar_types and saves as cluster_not_supported_calendar_types | |
| 14 | For each value in cluster_unsupported_calendar_types , TH writes the value to the ActiveCalendarType attributes | DUT returns CONSTRAINT_ERROR |

## Chapter 41. Binding Cluster Test Plan

## 41.1. PICS Definition

## 41.1.1. Role

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| BIND.S | Does the device implement the Binding Cluster as a server? | O | |
| BIND.C | Does the device implement the Binding Cluster as a client? | O | |

## 41.1.2. Server

## Attributes

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| BIND.S.A0000(Binding) | Does the DUT(server) support the Binding attribute? | BIND.S:M | |

## 41.1.3. Client

## Attributes

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |
| GRPKEY.C.A0000(Group KeyMap) | Does the DUT(client) have access privileges for the GroupKeyMap attribute implemented on the server? | BIND.C:O | |

| Variable | Description | Mandatory/Optional | Notes/Additional Constraints |

| OO.C.C00.Tx(Off) | Does the DUT(client) implement sending the Off command? | BIND.C:O |
| OO.C.C01.Tx(On) | Does the DUT(client) implement sending the On command? | BIND.C:O |
| GRPKEY.C.C00.Tx(KeyS etWrite) | Does the DUT(Client) implement sending KeySetWrite command? | BIND.C:O |
| G.C.C00.Tx(AddGroup) | Does the DUT(Client) implement sending AddGroup command? | BIND.C:O |

## 43.3.1. Testing tolerances

In test cases where a change in an attribute value is tested over time, it is permitted for the devices involved in the test to be within a tolerance of ±15% of the expected value. As such, these test cases indicate that the attribute value must be approximately equal to an expected value, to which the ±15% tolerance should then be applied. All other attribute values presented are expected to be exact.

## 43.3.2. Test steps manipulating attributes

In test case steps that require more than one attribute to be manipulated (e.g. read), the tester may decide whether it is appropriate or practical to send a single attribute manipulation command, containing multiple attributes, or multiple attribute manipulation commands, each containing a single attribute. The test case is designed to verify the behavior of the device supporting the attribute rather that verifying the attribute manipulation command in question.

## TC-S-2.2 Primary functionality with DUT as Server

## Purpose

This test case verifies the primary functionality of the Scenes Management Cluster server.

This test case requires an application configuration , AC , to be set on the device in order to create a scene. An AC is essentially a set of cluster attribute settings which affect the scene and is dependent on the application clusters supported on the server device. When the test calls for a specific ACi it is up to the tester to manipulate the attributes on the DUT according to the supported clusters such that each ACi is unique.

Since Scenes are using concepts from the Groups cluster, some commands from the Groups cluster are used in this test, e.g. AddGroup , AddGroupResponse and RemoveAllGroups .

## TC-S-2.3 Secondary functionality with DUT as Server

This test case requires an application configuration , AC , to be set on the device in order to create a scene. ## TC-ACL-2.4 ACL attribute[DUT-Commissionee]

## Purpose

1. Verify that Access Control cluster ACL attribute is present.
2. Verify that Access Control cluster ACL attribute accepts valid values.
3. Verify that Access Control cluster ACL attribute rejects invalid values.
4. Verify that Access Control cluster ACL attribute respects constraints and length restrictions.

## PICS

- ACL.S

## Pre-Conditions

| # | Doc Ref | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | | | N1 is the node ID of TH1 |
| 2 | | | CAT1 is a valid CAT with arbitrary ID and arbitrary version |
| 3 | | | CAT2 is a valid CAT with arbitrary ID and arbitrary version |
| 4 | | | CAT3 is a valid CAT with arbitrary ID and arbitrary version |
| 5 | | | CAT4 is a valid CAT with arbitrary ID and arbitrary version |

NOTE CATs are in the range 0xFFFF\_FFFD\_xxxx\_xxxx

The # column matches the test\_plan\_number values emitted by the Python certification test TC\_BRBINFO\_2\_1 , which uses the shared binfo\_attributes\_verification step list ( TestStep(0) through TestStep(29) ). Bridged Device Basic Information does not implement every Basic Information attribute; the harness still advances steps 1 (DataModelRevision), 7 (Location), 17 (LocalConfigDisabled), 20 (CapabilityMinima), 22 (SpecificationVersion), and 23 (MaxPathsPerInvoke), which are skipped when those attributes are absent on this cluster. Those step numbers are intentionally omitted from the table below; numbering is non-sequential to remain aligned with the script output.

## TC-BRBINFO-4.1 Verification of KeepActive Command [DUT-Server]

## Purpose

Verify the KeepActive has been implemented correctly on the DUT.

## PICS

- BRBINFO.S.C80.Rsp(KeepActive)

## Precondition

| # | Ref | Condition | Notes |
| 1 | | DUT (bridge) and TH can interact with each other on fabric one. DUT is commissioned. | |
| 2 | | Bridged TH_ICD and TH can interact with each other on fabric one. TH_ICD is commissioned. | |

| # | Ref | Condition | Notes |
| 3 | | Bridged TH_ICD devices of a supported type is commissioned to DUT (bridge) on fabric two. | |

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | Test harness which will be used to send and receive events and messages to the DUT |
| 2 | DUT | DUT which will send events to the TH |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on fabric one TH and TH\_ICD are on fabric one DUT and TH\_ICD are on fabric two

## Test Procedure

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | TH reads from the TH_ICD the IdleModeDuration , ActiveModeDuration , and ActiveModeThreshold attributes. | Store the values of IdleModeDuration , ActiveModeDuration , and ActiveModeThreshold . |
| 2 | • TH subscribes to ActiveChanged event from DUT with MinIntervalFloor set to 0 and isUrgent set to True | • TH validates subscription is successful |
| 3 | • TH sends the KeepActive command to DUT. ◦ StayActiveDuration: 1000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 29999 (invalid) | • Command returns ConstraintError |
| 4 | • TH sends the KeepActive command to DUT. ◦ StayActiveDuration: 1000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 3600001 (invalid) | • Command returns ConstraintError |
| 5 | • TH sends the KeepActive command to DUT. ◦ StayActiveDuration: 1000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 30000 (30s) | • Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) for KeepActive command |

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 6 | • TH registers for check-in from TH_ICD device and waits to receive check-in • TH checks its subscription to ActiveChanged event from DUT has yielded one new event within 5 seconds | • Verify that TH receives ActiveChanged event from DUT when TH_ICD device becomes active in less than IdleModeDuration • Verify the data of the ActiveChanged event received by TH contains a PromisedActiveDuration >= 1000 |
| 7 | • TH sends the KeepActive command to DUT. ◦ StayActiveDuration: 1000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 3600000 | • Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) for KeepActive command |
| 8 | • TH registers for check-in from TH_ICD device and waits to receive check-in • TH checks it's subscription to ActiveChanged event from DUT has yielded one new event within 5 seconds | • Verify that TH receives ActiveChanged event from DUT when TH_ICD device becomes active in less than IdleModeDuration • Verify the data of the ActiveChanged event received by TH contains a PromisedActiveDuration >= 1000 |
| 9 | • TH prevents TH_ICD from sending sending check-ins • TH sends the KeepActive command to DUT three times ◦ StayActiveDuration: 2000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 60000 (60s) | • Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) for each of the 3 _KeepActive command_s |
| 10 | • TH allows TH_ICD to resume sending check-ins • TH registers for check-in from TH_ICD device and waits to receive check-in • TH checks it's subscription to ActiveChanged event from DUT has yielded one new event within 5 | • Verify that TH receives ActiveChanged event once from DUT when TH_ICD device becomes active in less than IdleModeDuration • Verify the data of the ActiveChanged event received by TH contains a PromisedActiveDuration >= 2000 |

| # | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 12 | • TH prevents TH_ICD from sending sending check-ins • TH sends KeepActive command to DUT ◦ StayActiveDuration: 2000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 30000 (30s) | • Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) for KeepActive command |
| 13 | • Wait for 30s • TH allows TH_ICD to resume sending check-ins | |
| 14 | • TH registers for check-in from TH_ICD device and waits to receive two check- ins • TH checks its subscription to ActiveChanged event from DUT | • Subscription to ActiveChanged event has not yielded any new events since step 10. |
| 15 | • TH prevents TH_ICD from sending sending check-ins • TH sends KeepActive command to DUT ◦ StayActiveDuration: 2000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 30000 (30s) | • Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) for KeepActive command |
| 16 | • Wait 15s • TH sends KeepActive command to DUT ◦ StayActiveDuration: 2000 ◦ TimeoutMs: 60000 (60s) | • Verify DUT responds w/ status SUCCESS(0x00) for KeepActive command |
| 17 | • Wait for 15s • TH allows TH_ICD to resume sending check-ins | |
| 18 | • TH registers for check-in from TH_ICD device and waits to receive check-in | • TH checks its subscription to ActiveChanged event has yielded one new event. |

## Notes/Testing Considerations

- Waiting 5 seconds for event from DUT, after receiving check-in directly from TH\_ICD, should be enough time for the event to propagate.

## TC-TCTL-3.3 Optional temperature level functionality with DUT as Server

## Purpose

This test case verifies the optional functionality of the Temperature Control Cluster server. This test case is only required if the TL feature is supported (TCTL.S.F01(TL)).

## PICS

- TCTL.S
- TCTL.S.F01(TL)

## Spec References

{REF\_TCTL}.5 &amp; {REF\_TCTL}.7 - Refer to the *Temperature Control Cluster attribute and command* section.

## Required Devices

| # | Device Name | Device Description |
| 1 | TH | TH as Client. |
| 2 | DUT | DUT as Server. |

## Device Topology

TH and DUT are on the same fabric.

## Test Setup

Commission DUT to TH (can be skipped if done in a preceding test).

## Test Procedure

| # | PICS | Test Step | Expected Outcome |
| 1 | | Commission DUT to TH | |
| 2 | | Operate device such that a temperature level can be accepted | |
| 3 | | TH reads from the DUT the SupportedTemperatureLevels attribute | Save result list as supportedLevels |

| 4 | | TH sends command {C_SET_TEMPERATURE_COMMAND} with a value from supportedLevels saved as setLevel | Verify that the DUT response contains SUCCESS |
| 5 | | After a few seconds, TH reads from the DUT the SelectedTemperatureLevel attribute | Value is the same setLevel written in step 4 |
| 6 | TCTL.S.M .Supports InvalidIn State | Operate device such that a temperature level cannot be accepted | |
| 7 | TCTL.S.M .Supports InvalidIn State | TH sends command {C_SET_TEMPERATURE_COMMAND} with a value from supportedLevels that is different from setLevel | Verify that the DUT response contains CONSTRAINT_ERROR |
| 8 | TCTL.S.M .Supports InvalidIn State | after a few seconds, TH reads from the DUT the SelectedTemperatureLevel attribute | Value is the same setLevel written in step 4 |
